name: Poison Water
summary: In Mulgore, tainted wells threaten the water that sustains the tauren and local wildlife. Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village asks young Horde defenders to gather parts from the plains for a cleansing totem.

sections.title: A Land Desecrated
sections.body: Goblin interlopers and their lackeys have tainted Mulgore's wells, threatening the water that sustains the tauren tribes and local wildlife. Mull Thunderhorn, an elder in Bloodhoof Village, has discovered the pollution. For the tauren, who recently settled here, the wells are vital to life on these sacred plains.

sections.title: Gathering Nature's Essence
sections.body: Mull turns to tauren shamanism to cleanse the Winterhoof Water Well. He needs a ritual totem made with the strength of Mulgore's native beasts. You gather paws from prairie wolves and talons from mature plainstriders on the southwestern plains, bringing the land's own strength to bear against the pollution.

faq.q: Who poisoned the water wells in Mulgore?
faq.answer: Goblin interlopers and their lackeys have tainted Mulgore's sacred wells, threatening the water that sustains the tauren and local wildlife.

faq.q: Why does Mull Thunderhorn need wolf paws and plainstrider talons?
faq.answer: Mull uses prairie wolf paws and plainstrider talons to make a cleansing totem rooted in the strength of Mulgore's native beasts.

faq.q: Which well does this quest prepare to cleanse?
faq.answer: The gathered parts will make a cleansing totem for the Winterhoof Water Well.

aliases: where to turn in poison water
faq.answer: Mull Thunderhorn is in Bloodhoof Village, the main tauren settlement in central Mulgore, near Stonebull Lake.

faq.q: Where can the necessary wolves and plainstriders be found?
faq.answer: Prairie wolves and adult plainstriders roam the plains southwest of Bloodhoof Village.

faq.q: What happens after Mull receives the paws and talons?
faq.answer: Mull binds the paws and talons into a Winterhoof Cleansing Totem, then sends you to the Winterhoof Water Well to perform the purification rite.

angles.text: For a tauren, poisoned fresh water violates the Earth Mother's gifts. Cleansing the wells is a duty as you come of age in Mulgore.
For a shaman, restoring polluted water with a totem made from beast parts reflects tauren shamanism and its bond with local wildlife.
For a druid, goblins poisoning fresh springs threatens Mulgore's natural balance. You must protect its fragile flora and fauna.
